newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese metals demand seen affecting LME prices.
newsitem.headline: Chinese metals demand seen affecting LME prices.

text.p: A post-holiday spike in Chinese demand for base metals should impact prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders in Asia said on Monday.
That spike was visible as values on the Shanghai Metal Exchange soared when trading opened for the first time in two weeks, as China got back to work following the Lunar New Year holiday.

Shanghai copper futures opened sharply up with the most active May 1997 contract opening at 21,980 yuan ($2,648) per tonne, up 400 yuan. It rose further to its limit-up of 22,100 yuan per tonne early in the session.
Aluminium also opened up, with the May contract starting at 15,900 yuan per tonne, up 20 yuan.
A Japanese trader in Singapore said he expected aluminium's LME correction to continue as profit-taking came into play.
However, another source in Hong Kong said that LME aluminium is now at the bottom end of its correction and Chinese demand should give it impetus for another rise.
On Friday LME aluminium sagged under commission house sales and disappointed liquidation after the market failed to respond to a 9,975-tonne stock draw.
Final kerb trade was at $1,565, down $11 per tonne.
"Currently it (LME aluminium) is still at the lower end of the overall correction and when the Chinese open up I think there will be some support," the Hong Kong source said.
